name: Outpatients and clinics
oneLine: Keeps referrals, bookings, waiting lists and clinic days visible and moving.
today: Referrals sit in inboxes and paper books. There is no single waiting list. Everyone is booked for the start of clinic, slots go unfilled, and nobody chases who did not attend.
withOspeli: Every referral lands on one list with its wait shown. Clinic templates set slots, reminders go out, and check-in times are logged, so waits, empty slots and did-not-attend show clearly.

people.does: Checks patients in by code on a tablet, marks arrived, seen or did not attend.
Works the referral list, books slots from templates, sends reminders, rebooks cancellations.
Calls the next patient from the clinic queue on a phone, marks start and finish.
Reviews waiting lists, slot use and clinic start times; adjusts templates.
Sees waits by service and clinics cancelled or running short.

screens.name: Clinic queue (phone)
screens.shows: Today's patients by anonymous code: booked time, arrived, waiting time, called, finished.

screens.name: Referral and waiting list
screens.shows: All open referrals by service and wait, unbooked first, with oldest waits highlighted.

screens.name: Clinic templates
screens.shows: Slot patterns per clinic and day, new and follow-up slots, held and released slots.

screens.name: Clinic day summary
screens.shows: Slots used, empty, cancelled and did not attend, start time and overrun per clinic.

captures: Referral received and accepted: starts the waiting-time clock.
Appointment booked, rebooked or cancelled, with who cancelled: shows churn.
Reminder sent and reply: links reminders to attendance.
Patient arrived and checked in: starts the in-clinic wait.
Called in and consultation finished: measures in-clinic wait and clinic overrun.
Did not attend recorded: drives the did-not-attend rate and rebooking.
Clinic cancelled or reduced at short notice, with reason: shows lost capacity.

kpis.name: Did-not-attend rate
kpis.definition: appointments marked did not attend / appointments booked

kpis.name: Slot utilisation
kpis.definition: slots used / slots available in the template

kpis.name: Referral to first appointment
kpis.definition: referral accepted → first appointment attended, median by service

kpis.name: Waiting time in clinic
kpis.definition: patient checked in → called in, median per clinic

kpis.name: Clinic start punctuality
kpis.definition: clinics starting within the set window of scheduled time / clinics held

guide: When a clinic's did-not-attend rate rises above its usual range, suggests extra reminders or a booking review for that clinic, citing recent weeks.
When slots stay empty within two days of clinic, suggests offering them to the longest waiting referrals for that service.
When patients are all booked for the clinic start, suggests a staggered template, showing the current arrival-to-called waits.
playbooks: Waiting list validation: check each open referral, output list cleaned and contacted.
Clinic template review: compare demand and slots, output a revised template.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_clinics_list_waiting
agentCommands.does: List open referrals by service and wait, unbooked first, with filters and limit.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_clinics_find_slots
agentCommands.does: Find free slots for a service and date range, with clinic and time.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_clinics_book_appointment
agentCommands.does: Propose booking a referral into a slot; booking clerk confirms.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_clinics_record_attendance
agentCommands.does: Record arrived, called, finished or did not attend for an appointment code.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_clinics_get_day_summary
agentCommands.does: Return a clinic day's slots used, empty, cancelled and waits.

standards: JCI Access to Care and Continuity of Care (ACC)
HL7 FHIR Appointment, Slot and Schedule resources
notFor: Does not decide clinical urgency of referrals or who needs follow-up. Never times or ranks individual clinicians.

name: Emergency department flow
oneLine: Shows every wait in the emergency department, from arrival to departure.
today: Times are written on paper or not at all. Ambulances wait at the door, cubicles fill with patients waiting for ward beds, and nobody can say where the hours went.
withOspeli: Each stage is a timestamped tap: arrival, triage, seen, decision, bed requested, departed. A live board shows waits and blocks, and admission requests reach the bed board at once.

people.does: Sees the live board, logs arrivals and stage changes, raises escalation in two taps.
Records triage time and the category staff assigned, on a phone.
Sees decisions to admit waiting for beds and matches them on the bed board.
Sees handover status and time waiting at the door.
Watches crowding, long waits and escalation level; leads the full-capacity response.

screens.name: Department board
screens.shows: Patients by anonymous code and area: stage, time since arrival, waiting for what.

screens.name: Log a stage (phone)
screens.shows: Pick a patient code, tap the next stage; time is stamped automatically.

screens.name: Waiting for a bed
screens.shows: Decisions to admit by specialty, time waiting, bed requested and bed offered.

screens.name: Ambulance handover
screens.shows: Ambulances arrived, handed over and still waiting, with time at the door.

screens.name: Escalation status
screens.shows: Current crowding level, triggers met, actions taken and who decided.

captures: Arrival and arrival mode: starts every time measure.
Ambulance arrived and handover completed: measures time at the door.
Triage time and staff-assigned category: measures time to triage.
First seen by a clinician: measures time to be seen.
Decision to admit and bed requested: starts the wait for a bed.
Departure and destination, or left before being seen: ends the stay.
Escalation level changed, with triggers and decision maker: records the response.

kpis.name: national time standard
kpis.definition: attendances departing within 4 hours of arrival / all attendances
kpis.source: National emergency department time standard (set locally)

kpis.name: Time to triage
kpis.definition: arrival → triage recorded, median

kpis.name: Decision to admit to departure
kpis.definition: decision to admit → left the department, median and over 12 hours

kpis.name: Ambulance handover time
kpis.definition: ambulance arrived → handover completed, median and over the local limit

kpis.name: Left before being seen
kpis.definition: attendances leaving before first seen / all attendances

guide: When decisions to admit wait longer than the set limit, suggests a bed meeting review, listing waits by specialty from the bed board.
When crowding triggers are met, suggests the matching escalation level and actions for the charge nurse to confirm.
When ambulances wait beyond the local handover limit, alerts the operations manager with current cubicle and corridor use.
playbooks: Department flow walk: time each stage, output the biggest wait.
Full-capacity drill: run the escalation steps, output actions and timings.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_ed_get_board
agentCommands.does: Return the live department board by area, stage and wait, using patient codes.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_ed_log_stage
agentCommands.does: Record a stage change for a patient code with event time.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_ed_list_awaiting_beds
agentCommands.does: List decisions to admit waiting for beds, with time and specialty.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_ed_propose_escalation
agentCommands.does: Propose an escalation level with triggers met; the charge nurse decides.

standards: National emergency department time standard (set locally)
JCI Access to Care and Continuity of Care (ACC)
notFor: Does not triage, assign categories, or decide who is seen first. Measures waits by stage, never individual staff.

name: Beds, admissions and discharge
oneLine: One live picture of every bed, admission and discharge across the organisation.
today: Bed state lives on whiteboards and phone calls. Discharges are decided late, then wait for medicines, transport or family. Beds sit empty but dirty while patients wait downstairs.
withOspeli: A live bed board shows each bed as occupied, ready, dirty or blocked. Expected discharge dates and delay reasons are logged, and a discharge triggers cleaning, so delays show and beds turn faster.

people.does: Updates bed state on a phone, sets expected discharge dates, records delay reasons.
Matches bed requests to ready beds and proposes moves for the ward to accept.
Records admissions, transfers and discharges with event times.
Tracks patients ready to leave and what each is waiting for.
Runs the bed meeting from the board; sees occupancy, delays and long stays.

screens.name: Bed board
screens.shows: Every bed by ward: occupied, ready, dirty or blocked, with patient code and time in state.

screens.name: My ward (phone)
screens.shows: Ward beds, expected discharge dates, delay reasons and pending admissions, updated in taps.

screens.name: Bed requests
screens.shows: Requests from the emergency department, theatres and transfers, waiting time and bed offered.

screens.name: Discharge tracker
screens.shows: Patients ready to leave, what they wait for: medicines, transport, placement, family.

screens.name: Bed meeting view
screens.shows: Occupancy, expected discharges today, delays over 48 hours and long stays by ward.

captures: Bed requested and bed allocated: measures the wait for a bed.
Admission, transfer and discharge times: drive occupancy and length of stay.
Expected discharge date set or changed: shows planning and slippage.
Ready to leave and actual departure: measures discharge delay.
Delay reason by category: shows what holds discharges.
Bed vacated, cleaned and ready: drives bed turnaround.
Bed blocked or closed, with reason: shows lost capacity.

kpis.name: Bed occupancy
kpis.definition: occupied bed-days / available bed-days

kpis.name: Average length of stay
kpis.definition: inpatient bed-days / discharges in period

kpis.name: Discharges before noon
kpis.definition: discharges before 12:00 / all discharges

kpis.name: Discharge delay
kpis.definition: ready to leave → departed, total delayed days and over 48 hours

kpis.name: Long-stay patients
kpis.definition: inpatients with stays of 7 or more and 21 or more days / inpatients

guide: When a patient's expected discharge date passes with no delay reason, prompts the ward to record one.
When several patients ready to leave wait for the same thing, such as transport, flags the shared cause to the discharge coordinator.
When bed requests wait and beds sit dirty, suggests which cleans to request first, citing bed requests.
playbooks: Daily bed meeting: review board and delays, output actions with owners.
Long-stay review: list 21-day-plus stays by delay reason, output actions.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_beds_find_free
agentCommands.does: Find ready beds by ward and bed type, with time ready.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_beds_propose_allocation
agentCommands.does: Propose a bed for a bed request with reasons; the ward accepts.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_beds_update_state
agentCommands.does: Set a bed's state or a patient code's expected discharge date.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_beds_list_delays
agentCommands.does: List patients ready to leave and their delay reasons, by ward.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_beds_get_summary
agentCommands.does: Return occupancy, expected discharges and long stays for the bed meeting.

standards: JCI Access to Care and Continuity of Care (ACC)
HL7 FHIR Encounter and Location resources
notFor: Does not decide fitness for discharge or who gets a bed on clinical grounds. Never scores wards or staff.

name: Theatres and procedure lists
oneLine: Makes every theatre and procedure session start on time and run full.
today: Lists are set late and change on the day. Sessions start late waiting for a bed, a missing tray or staff. Cancellations happen after patients are prepared, and turnaround time is a guess.
withOspeli: Lists, sessions and each case's key times are logged in taps. Readiness checks show missing beds, kit or staff the day before, and cancellations carry reasons, so lost session time is visible.

people.does: Builds and changes lists, checks readiness, records cancellations and reasons.
Taps patient in, procedure start, finish and out on a phone.
Sees trays needed per list and flags kit not ready.
Reviews session use, late starts, cancellations and turnaround by theatre.
Sees sessions unused, cancellations for lack of beds, and lists at risk.

screens.name: Today's lists
screens.shows: Each theatre's sessions and cases by patient code, current stage, running late or early.

screens.name: Case times (phone)
screens.shows: Tap into room, anaesthesia start, procedure start, finish, out of room; stamped automatically.

screens.name: Readiness check
screens.shows: Tomorrow's cases: bed, kit, staff and checklist status, gaps highlighted.

screens.name: Session review
screens.shows: Planned versus used time, late start, early finish, turnaround and cancellations per session.

captures: Session planned, released or unused: shows capacity offered and lost.
Patient in room, procedure start and finish, out: measures session use.
Late start with reason: shows what delays the first case.
Cancellation on the day, with reason category: shows avoidable losses.
Out of room to next patient in: measures turnaround.
Tray or kit not ready: links sterile services to delays.
Surgical safety checklist completed, yes or no: tracks completion.

kpis.name: Session utilisation
kpis.definition: time patients in theatre within planned session / planned session time

kpis.name: Late starts
kpis.definition: sessions where first case starts after the set window / sessions held

kpis.name: Cancellations on the day
kpis.definition: cases cancelled on the day / cases listed

kpis.name: Turnaround time
kpis.definition: patient out of room → next patient in room, median

kpis.name: Checklist completion
kpis.definition: cases with the surgical safety checklist recorded complete / cases

guide: When tomorrow's case has no bed booked or kit ready, flags it to the theatre coordinator with the gap.
When sessions are released late repeatedly for a service, suggests a review of session allocation, citing release dates.
When cancellations for one reason rise, suggests a short review of that cause, with the cases listed by code.
playbooks: Session review: compare planned and used time, output lost time by cause.
Cancellation review: group last month's cancellations, output top avoidable causes.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_theatres_get_lists
agentCommands.does: Return today's or a date's lists by theatre, with case stages and delays.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_theatres_log_case_time
agentCommands.does: Record a case milestone time for a patient code.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_theatres_check_readiness
agentCommands.does: List next-day cases missing a bed, kit, staff or checklist.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_theatres_propose_list_change
agentCommands.does: Propose moving or swapping a case; the theatre coordinator decides.

notFor: Does not decide which patient is operated on first or clinical fitness. Never times or ranks individual surgeons.

name: Diagnostics: imaging and laboratory
oneLine: Tracks every request, sample and scan from order to reported result.
today: Samples get lost between ward and lab. Nobody can say when a scan will happen. An analyser or scanner goes down and wards find out by phoning. Results wait to be seen.
withOspeli: Requests, specimens and scans carry timestamps at each handoff. Wards see status without phoning, downtime is posted on the board, and turnaround is measured per test and step.

people.does: Sees request status by patient code: collected, received, done, reported.
Scans specimens in, records rejections and reasons, sees the analyser queue.
Sees the scan list, marks scanned and sent for report on a phone.
Reviews turnaround, backlogs, rejections and equipment downtime.
Sees diagnostic waits holding discharges, theatres or the emergency department.

screens.name: Request tracker (phone)
screens.shows: Requests by patient code and stage: ordered, collected, received, done, reported.

screens.name: Specimen log
screens.shows: Specimens received by time and source, rejected with reason, missing after collection.

screens.name: Imaging list
screens.shows: Requests waiting by modality and age, booked slots, scanned and waiting for report.

screens.name: Equipment status
screens.shows: Analysers and scanners up or down, since when, linked work order and expected return.

captures: Request made, with source and urgency set by requester: starts turnaround.
Specimen collected and received in lab: shows transport time and losses.
Specimen rejected, with reason: drives rejection rate and fixes.
Result validated or scan reported: ends turnaround.
Scan booked and performed: measures request to scan.
Analyser or scanner down and back: shows downtime and its impact.
Critical result phoned, time recorded: tracks notification time.

kpis.name: Laboratory turnaround time
kpis.definition: specimen received → result validated, median and percentile, by test

kpis.name: Request to report (imaging)
kpis.definition: request made → report issued, median by modality

kpis.name: Specimen rejection rate
kpis.definition: specimens rejected / specimens received

kpis.name: Equipment downtime
kpis.definition: hours down / scheduled hours, per analyser or scanner

kpis.name: Reporting backlog
kpis.definition: scans performed and not yet reported, by age band

guide: When a specimen is collected but not received within the set time, prompts the ward and lab to check it.
When an analyser or scanner goes down, posts the status to affected wards and suggests the agreed backup route.
When rejections for one reason rise from one area, suggests a short review with that area, citing the reasons.
playbooks: Turnaround walk: time a sample's journey, output the longest step.
Downtime drill: rehearse backup routes, output gaps and actions.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_diagnostics_get_request_status
agentCommands.does: Return status and timestamps for requests by patient code or area.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_diagnostics_log_specimen
agentCommands.does: Record a specimen collected, received or rejected, with reason.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_diagnostics_list_backlog
agentCommands.does: List waiting scans or tests by modality, age and area.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_diagnostics_set_equipment_status
agentCommands.does: Propose marking equipment down or up, linked to a work order.

standards: WHO Laboratory Quality Management System (LQMS) Handbook
HL7 FHIR ServiceRequest, Specimen and DiagnosticReport resources
notFor: Does not interpret results, decide tests or prioritise patients clinically. Never times individual scientists or radiographers.

name: Pharmacy operations
oneLine: Keeps medicines in stock and dispensing moving, so nobody waits needlessly.
today: Stock is counted by hand and runs out without warning. Discharge medicines are requested late and patients wait hours to go home. Expired stock is found too late.
withOspeli: Stock levels, top-up points and expiry dates are tracked by location. Dispensing requests are timestamped, so discharge medicine waits show live, and stock-outs are warned before they happen.

people.does: Scans stock in and out, works the dispensing queue, marks ready.
Requests discharge medicines early and sees when they will be ready.
Sees the dispensing queue by request time, checks and releases items.
Reviews stock-outs, expiries, top-up levels and dispensing turnaround.
Sees which planned discharges wait for medicines.

screens.name: Dispensing queue
screens.shows: Requests by ward and request time: received, in progress, checked, ready, collected.

screens.name: Discharge medicines (phone)
screens.shows: For a ward: requests made, expected ready time, ready for collection.

screens.name: Stock levels
screens.shows: Items by location against top-up level, stock-outs, days of stock left.

screens.name: Expiry watch
screens.shows: Items expiring within the set window, by location, with quantity.

captures: Dispensing request received: starts turnaround.
Item checked and ready, then collected: ends turnaround, shows collection wait.
Stock below top-up level: triggers reorder before a stock-out.
Stock-out start and end, by item: drives availability and duration.
Stock expired or wasted: shows avoidable loss.
Stock received from supplier or stores: links to supply delays.

kpis.name: Discharge medicines turnaround
kpis.definition: request received → ready for collection, median

kpis.name: Tracer medicine availability
kpis.definition: tracer items in stock on the day / tracer items listed

kpis.name: Stock-out duration
kpis.definition: days out of stock per item, in period

kpis.name: Expiry value
kpis.definition: value of stock expired / value of stock held, in period

guide: When stock will reach zero before the next delivery at current use, suggests a reorder quantity for the pharmacy manager.
When discharge medicine requests arrive late in the day, suggests earlier requests for that ward, citing request times.
When items near expiry, suggests moving them to areas that use them faster.
playbooks: Stock count: count by location, output variances and top-up updates.
Discharge medicines review: map request to collection, output main delay.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_pharmacy_list_queue
agentCommands.does: List dispensing requests by ward, type and wait.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_pharmacy_get_stock
agentCommands.does: Return stock levels, top-up levels and days left by item or location.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_pharmacy_propose_reorder
agentCommands.does: Draft a reorder from use and stock; the pharmacy manager approves.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_pharmacy_mark_ready
agentCommands.does: Mark a dispensing request ready for collection.

standards: WHO Model List of Essential Medicines
notFor: Does not choose medicines, doses or substitutions, or check prescriptions clinically. Never ranks individual pharmacy staff.

name: Maternity and children's flow
oneLine: Shows maternity beds, cots and children's beds live, with transfers tracked.
today: Nobody knows how many cots are free until someone phones round. Units close to admissions with little notice. Transfers out are arranged by phone and nobody records why.
withOspeli: Live boards show labour rooms, maternity beds, cots and children's beds. Closures and transfers are logged with reasons and times, and mother and baby codes stay linked across moves.

people.does: Updates rooms, beds and cots on a phone; records closures and reasons.
Updates cot state and staffing, logs transfers in and out.
Updates children's beds and expected discharges.
Sees capacity across units and arranges transfer requests.
Sees closures, transfers out for lack of capacity, and trends.

screens.name: Maternity and children's board
screens.shows: Labour rooms, maternity beds, cots and children's beds: occupied, ready, closed.

screens.name: My unit (phone)
screens.shows: Unit rooms, beds or cots, staffed status and pending admissions, updated in taps.

screens.name: Transfers
screens.shows: Transfer requests in and out, reason category, requested, accepted, departed.

screens.name: Closures log
screens.shows: Each closure to admissions, start and end time, reason and who decided.

captures: Room, bed or cot occupied, ready or closed: drives capacity.
Unit closed or reopened to admissions, with reason: shows lost capacity.
Transfer requested, accepted and completed, with reason category: shows delays.
Transfer out for lack of cot or bed: shows capacity gaps.
Mother and baby codes linked: keeps moves together without names.
Admission and discharge with event times: drives occupancy and stay.

kpis.name: Cot occupancy
kpis.definition: occupied cot-days / available cot-days

kpis.name: Unit closure hours
kpis.definition: hours closed to admissions / hours in period, per unit

kpis.name: Transfers out for capacity
kpis.definition: transfers out for lack of cot or bed / all transfers out

kpis.name: Transfer request to departure
kpis.definition: transfer requested → patient departed, median

guide: When cots or beds will run short at expected admissions, alerts the flow coordinator early, citing the board.
When a unit closes repeatedly for the same reason, suggests a review of that cause with the manager.
When a transfer request waits beyond the set time, prompts escalation to the named role.
playbooks: Capacity review: closures and transfers out by cause, output actions.
Transfer walk: map a transfer from request to arrival, output delays.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_maternity_get_capacity
agentCommands.does: Return labour rooms, beds and cots by state and unit.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_maternity_log_closure
agentCommands.does: Record a unit closure or reopening with reason and decision maker.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_maternity_list_transfers
agentCommands.does: List transfer requests by stage, reason and wait.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_maternity_propose_transfer_route
agentCommands.does: Propose a receiving unit with free capacity; a named person decides.

standards: WHO Standards for Improving Quality of Maternal and Newborn Care in Health Facilities
JCI Access to Care and Continuity of Care (ACC)

name: Critical care capacity
oneLine: Shows critical care beds, delayed step-downs and transfers out, live.
today: Critical care is full while patients ready to step down wait for ward beds. Surgery is cancelled for lack of a bed. Transfers out happen at night and are not counted.
withOspeli: A live board shows critical care beds, staffed status and patients ready to step down. Delays waiting for ward beds are timed and transfers out for capacity are logged with reasons.

people.does: Updates beds and staffed status, marks patients ready to step down.
Sees step-down requests and finds ward beds on the bed board.
Sees critical care beds booked for planned surgery and their risk.
Reviews occupancy, step-down delays and transfers out for capacity.
Sees critical care capacity in the daily bed meeting and escalations.

screens.name: Critical care board
screens.shows: Beds by state: occupied, ready, closed; staffed or not; ready to step down.

screens.name: Step-down tracker
screens.shows: Patients ready to step down, hours waiting, ward bed requested and offered.

screens.name: Planned admissions
screens.shows: Beds booked for planned surgery today and tomorrow, confirmed or at risk.

screens.name: Update unit (phone)
screens.shows: Bed and staffing state, ready-to-step-down flag, admissions expected, in taps.

captures: Bed occupied, ready, closed or unstaffed: drives true capacity.
Ready to step down and left the unit: measures step-down delay.
Ward bed requested for step-down: links to the bed board.
Planned surgery bed booked, used or cancelled: shows impact on theatres.
Transfer out for lack of capacity, with time: shows capacity gaps.
Discharge to ward out of hours: shows when step-downs happen.

kpis.definition: occupied bed-days / staffed bed-days

kpis.name: Step-down delay

kpis.name: Out-of-hours discharges

kpis.name: Planned surgery cancelled for lack of critical care bed
kpis.definition: cancellations for that reason / planned cases needing a bed

guide: When patients wait to step down beyond the set limit, raises their ward bed requests at the bed meeting.
When planned surgery needs a bed and none is expected free, alerts the theatre coordinator a day ahead.
When out-of-hours discharges rise, suggests reviewing the morning step-down routine, citing times.
playbooks: Step-down review: map ready to left unit, output main delays.
Capacity huddle: beds, staffing and demand, output actions with owners.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_criticalcare_get_capacity
agentCommands.does: Return beds by state and staffing, with ready-to-step-down count.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_criticalcare_list_stepdowns
agentCommands.does: List patient codes ready to step down, hours waiting and ward bed status.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_criticalcare_mark_ready
agentCommands.does: Record a patient code ready to step down, as decided by the team.

agentCommands.name: ospeli_criticalcare_propose_ward_bed
agentCommands.does: Propose a ward bed for a step-down; the ward accepts.

standards: JCI Access to Care and Continuity of Care (ACC)
HL7 FHIR Encounter and Location resources
notFor: Does not decide admission to, or readiness to leave, critical care. Never scores clinicians or units.

name: Mental health and long-stay beds
oneLine: Tracks mental health and long-stay beds, delayed transfers and placements.
today: Patients stay weeks after they are ready because a placement, home support or funding is not arranged. Beds are found far away by phone. Nobody counts the days lost.
withOspeli: A board shows mental health, rehabilitation and long-stay beds. Ready-to-leave dates, delay reasons and placement requests are logged, so lost bed-days and their causes are visible.

people.does: Updates bed state, records ready-to-leave dates and delay reasons on a phone.
Tracks placement and home support requests, chases each step.
Records placement and support progress against each patient code.
Sees free beds and placements far away, and arranges returns.
Reviews lost bed-days, delay causes and far-away placements.

screens.name: Bed board
screens.shows: Beds by unit and type: occupied, ready, closed; days since ready to leave.

screens.name: Delayed transfers
screens.shows: Patients ready to leave, days waiting and the reason category, by ward.

screens.name: Placements
screens.shows: Placement requests by stage: requested, assessed, funded, accepted, moved.

screens.name: Update ward (phone)
screens.shows: Bed states, ready dates and delay reasons, updated in taps.

captures: Ready to leave date recorded by the team: starts delay clock.
Delay reason category: shows what holds transfers.
Placement requested, assessed, funded, accepted: shows where requests wait.
Patient placed outside the usual area, start and end: shows far placements.
Admission and discharge with event times: drives occupancy and stay.
Bed closed with reason: shows lost capacity.

kpis.name: Delayed transfer days
kpis.definition: days from ready to leave → departure, summed per period

kpis.name: Patients delayed
kpis.definition: patients past ready to leave date / inpatients

kpis.name: Placement request to move

kpis.name: Out-of-area placement days

name: Health records and information
oneLine: Tracks where records are, how fast they arrive, and who accessed them.
today: Paper charts go missing before clinic. Duplicate patient numbers split one history. Coding runs weeks behind, and requests for records wait in an inbox with no clock.
withOspeli: Record requests and movements are tracked like work orders. Duplicates are flagged for merge review. Coding backlogs and release requests show their age. Every access is in the audit trail.

people.does: Scans a chart out and in by phone; works the pull list.

Works the coding queue by age and sees what is missing.
Handles release requests, access reviews and breach reports.
Monitors retrieval times, duplicates, backlog and retention schedules.

name: Planning, business cases, capital projects
oneLine: Builds business cases from real data and tracks capital projects to benefits.
today: Business cases are written from scratch with guessed figures. Approved projects drift without a clear owner. Department redesigns open with no check that the promised benefits came.
withOspeli: Cases draw on the site's own time stamps, process maps and costs. Each project tracks milestones, budget, risks and actions. After go-live, the same KPIs show whether benefits came.

people.does: Starts a case from a problem, attaching process maps and current KPIs.
Updates milestones, risks and spend from a phone after site walks.
Adds space, utility and works estimates and the redesign layout.
Checks costs and funding sources before investment approval.
Compares cases, decides what goes forward, and reviews benefits after go-live.

Department redesign: current map, future map, layout, capacity check.

name: Finance, costing and budgets
oneLine: Shows each department its budget, spend and cost per case, with reasons.
today: Budget reports arrive weeks after month end, in spreadsheets few managers read. Overspends surface too late, and nobody can link cost to the beds, theatre lists or staffing behind it.
withOspeli: Spend sits beside activity from the event log, so cost per bed-day or case uses the same counts as operations. Designed to flag variances early, with the likely driver and an owner.

people.does: Checks budget versus actual on phone, explains variances, approves spend requests.
Sees temporary staffing spend for the ward this week before booking more.
Loads ledger extracts, maps cost centres, agrees variance notes with managers.
Reviews cost per case alongside flow, and approves recovery actions.
Sets budgets, signs off monthly position, owns the costing method.

oneLine: For sites that bill insurers, payers or patients: track every claim to payment.
today: Where care is billed, missing authorisations, uncaptured charges and rejected claims are found weeks later. Staff chase paper, cash arrives late, and nobody sees where claims get stuck.
withOspeli: An optional module, switched off by default. Each claim follows one timeline from registration to payment. Designed to surface missing steps before submission and route denials to the right queue.

people.does: Records coverage details and eligibility checks at arrival, on phone or desk.

Reviews days in accounts receivable and cash forecast in the monthly pack.

name: IT, digital and cyber
oneLine: Keeps systems, devices and access working, and plans for when they fail.
today: IT faults are reported by phone and forgotten. Nobody knows which systems are down, who still has access after leaving, or whether backups restore. Downtime means hunting for paper forms.
withOspeli: IT faults use the same work-order engine as facilities. A status board shows systems up or down; access, patches and backup tests are tracked. Downtime mode switches staff to printable fallbacks.

today: Each department counts differently, numbers are hand-tallied from registers, and external reports are rebuilt from scratch every month. Deadlines slip and nobody can trace a figure to its source.

name: Patient experience and feedback
oneLine: Logs complaints and feedback, tracks responses, and turns themes into actions.
today: Complaints arrive by letter, email, phone and in person, and some are lost. Responses run late, the same themes repeat, and nobody can show what changed.
withOspeli: Every complaint and comment gets one record, an owner and response timers. Themes link to the services and processes involved, and actions are tracked until done.

people.does: Logs complaints from any channel, assigns owners and chases responses.
Gets assigned complaints on a phone, records response and agreed actions.
Logs a concern or compliment at the desk in under a minute.
Reviews themes by service and links them to improvement actions.

name: Process mapping
oneLine: Maps how work really flows, step by step and role by role.
today: Process maps are sticky notes from a workshop, with guessed times. Nobody knows which wait is biggest, and changes are tried on the ward without testing first.
withOspeli: Teams map steps by role with waiting and hands-on time, see where time goes, and test a change on a proposed version first. Phone walk mode is coming, so times are measured.

people.does: Builds the current map with the team and tests a proposed version.
Walks a process on a phone, tapping each step as it happens (coming).
Compares today and proposed maps and decides which change to trial.
Maps the fault-to-fix process and spots handoffs that only pass information.

screens.name: Swimlane map
screens.shows: Steps in role lanes, wait and hands-on time on each, biggest waits highlighted.

screens.name: List view (phone)

screens.name: Today versus proposed
screens.shows: Total time, hands-on time, waiting share and handoffs, before and after a change.

screens.name: Guide panel
screens.shows: Where to look and why, with a try button that changes only the proposed map.

screens.name: Walk mode (phone, coming)

kpis.name: Total elapsed time

kpis.definition: Total waiting time / total elapsed time

guide: When one wait is a large share of the whole process, names it and asks what it waits for.
When steps only pass on information after long waits, suggests a one-tap status update instead.
When neighbouring steps by different roles have a long wait, asks if they could run together.
When steps have no times, suggests timing them on the next walk.

name: Playbooks
oneLine: Ready-made routines turn the day's events into the reports operations teams produce.
today: Every week someone rebuilds the same flow report, delay summary or business case from scratch, in a different spreadsheet, so results never compare week to week.
withOspeli: Each playbook has a fixed input, a fixed analysis and a ready-to-use output, run on the site's own data the same way every time, with each metric's definition beside its number.

people.does: Runs the daily flow report before the morning meeting.
